package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The article discusses general supply chain threats and how SLSA and Sonatype products address them, referencing historical incidents (e.g., event-stream, Webmin, Browserify typosquatting) as examples, but does not provide actual code or package-level details for any specific malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected modification of build artifacts not matching source repository
Introduction of dependencies with mismatched provenance or source
Typosquatting: package names similar to popular packages but with malicious intent
Sudden unavailability or removal of critical dependencies
file_indicators: Packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting)
Build artifacts with provenance not matching expected source control
Dependencies with missing or unverifiable provenance
network_indicators: Connections to untrusted or unexpected package mirrors
Downloads of packages from non-official or unverified repositories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose provenance does not match the expected source repository or builder. Flag and quarantine dependencies that appear in the build process but are not present in the official source control or have mismatched metadata. Detect and block packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting). Track and alert on sudden unavailability or removal of dependencies, and verify the integrity and source of all components before allowing them into the build pipeline.
